title: One-step transition for input movement
statement: Let $s,s'$ be states, let $ip$ be a valid input-head position on a Boolean input word $y$, let $v$ be a natural number, and let $q$ be an integer. Suppose that for every possible work-tape reading, the transition from state $s$ on the symbol read at input position $ip$ is the action that moves the input head by $mvI$, leaves the work tape unchanged, and enters state $s'$. Then one step of the doubled-input machine from the configuration with state $s$, input-head position $ip$, tape storing the binary expansion of $v$, and work-tape head at $q$ gives the configuration with state $s'$, input-head position moved by the clamped movement $mvI$, the same tape, and work-tape head still at $q$.
hypotheses_covered: $ip$ is a valid input-head position for $y$
For every work-tape reading, the transition from $s$ on the symbol at $ip$ equals the specified input-only movement action
